transcript:
This message comes from Kachava. A little boost goes a long way, especially when it comes to caring for your gut during the holiday season and beyond.
Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix in to your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to Kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Culver City, California, I'm Dua-Halee Sykowtow.
Thanksgiving travelers have had to face all kinds of challenges today.
From road closures to flight delays due to storms hitting both the east and west coast.
Flight aware shows more than 17,000 flights delayed so far with about
3,300 of those flights coming into the U.S. or going out. And Piers Windsor-Johnson reports coastal flooding has already hit parts of the mid-Atlantic region.
Forecasters say Wingus reached 60 miles an hour in parts of the mid-Atlantic, bringing down trees and knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of customers.
Some communities along the coast saw major flooding at the morning high tide. Rich Otto, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center,
says strong winds off the ocean have been pushing water towards shore.
There'll be another high tide cycle later on this evening along the east coast, which also bring another wave of coastal flooding.
However, I think that next week this evening won't be quite as significant as what we were seeing this morning.
Parts of southern New Jersey could end up with three to five inches of rain in New York City.
Winds are expected to ease overnight. Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
President Trump spent Thanksgiving Day calling deployed U.S. service members from his Florida estate today.
He thanked them for their service and offered encouraging words to troops far from home.
Later, he talked to reporters about the surprise reinstatement of Jensen Huang,
NVIDIA's CEO. Without him, I just don't know, you know, everybody's replaceable, I guess.
But I just thought I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock.
And I think it's a great thing that he's going back.
Stocks soared upon his return, then tumbled by Wednesday.
At least 31 people have been killed in a road accident in Cairo.
Egypt's health ministry says a truck carrying gas cylinders flipped on a highway and exploded,
and Paris Ayyebachari reports.
Egypt's public prosecutor says an initial investigation shows 27 cars and motorcycles caught fire
when a large truck carrying gas cylinders turned on its side and exploded into an inferno.
Prosecutors say they are now collecting DNA samples from the bodies to identify those killed.
Videos online showed a huge fire-raging Wednesday evening on the main ring road that connects Cairo with the city of Giza.
This is one of Egypt's deadliest road accidents in years.
Earlier this month, two trains collided just south of Cairo,
killing at least seven people and wounding more than 100. There are growing calls for the transport minister's resignation.
Ayyebachari, NPR News.
Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX has been given the green light by the Trump administration
to put about one million satellites or data centers in space.
You're listening to NPR News.
The future of a federal law that requires employers to provide reasonable accommodations for pregnancy and pregnancy-related conditions is in question.
As NPR's Andrea Shue reports, the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act faces multiple challenges.
This month, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals struck down the law on a technicality.
The court found not enough house lawmakers were present in the chamber when they passed the measure as part of a larger package in late 2022.
Under COVID-era rules, many members voted from home.
For now, the ruling only applies to the plaintiff in the case, the state of Texas.
Private employers must still comply with the law.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration is seeking to narrow the types of conditions covered by the law.
A proposed rule is expected soon.
Under current rules, employers have to provide reasonable accommodations for not just pregnancy and childbirth,
but also menopause and fertility-related conditions and others.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
The deadliest Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo, with more than 12,000 confirmed cases,
is made more complicated by escalating fighting between army and rebel groups.
Congo's Health Ministry says nearly 6,000 people have died from Ebola,
and the ongoing fighting prevents medical teams from reaching hard-hit communities.
A World Health Organization Ebola manager said several WHO personnel and Congolese health officials had to be evacuated to Boonia earlier this week after intense fighting.
I'm Dua Ali Saikoutel, NPR News.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone, offering an alternative approach to language learning.
The app guides users to intuitively think in a second language using images and contextual audio,
mimicking how people acquire speech as children.
The platform also includes advanced speech recognition technology that compares a learner's pronunciation directly with native speakers to refine accent precision.
Learn more about their immersion method and the new Rosetta Stone Sapphire app at RosettaStone.com.

topics.text: Thanksgiving travelers face thousands of flight delays and road closures from East and West Coast storms
Coastal flooding hits mid-Atlantic communities during morning high tide, with winds reaching 60 mph
Trump calls deployed U.S. service members from his Florida estate on Thanksgiving Day
Trump comments on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement, with stocks soaring then tumbling
At least 31 killed when gas cylinder truck overturns and explodes on Cairo ring road
Trump administration gives SpaceX approval to deploy about one million satellites in space
Fifth Circuit strikes down Pregnant Workers Fairness Act on technicality over House voting procedure
Trump administration moves to narrow conditions covered by the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act
Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo surpasses 12,000 cases as fighting hampers medical response
